title: The Iliad — Wrath, Sing, Goddess
description: Machine-readable mirror of a line-for-line English translation of Homer's Iliad. aligned-NN.jsonl is the parallel corpus for one book: one JSON object per verse line, {book, line, greek, en}, in the printed order of the Monro-Allen text, English verse only (no note markers). book-NN.txt is the full translation source for one book: a one-line argument, the translator's commentary, numbered verse lines ('  123  text', one English line per Greek line, same numbering as the Greek) with bracketed [7] markers pointing into a notes section of scholarly endnotes, each opening with its (book.line) reference. registry.json is the index of names: the poem's principal persons, gods, peoples, and places, with category, aliases, note, and 'book.line' refs. Cite passages as book.line, e.g. 6.146. Human-readable edition with line anchors: /read/book-NN.html#L123.
license: English translation (the 'en' fields and the verse in book-NN.txt): CC0 1.0 (public domain dedication). Notes, commentary, and index: CC BY 4.0, (c) 2026 Chris Duffy. Greek: Monro-Allen, Oxford Classical Text, 1920 (public domain).

books.argument: The plague; Agamemnon takes Achilles' prize, the girl Briseis, and Achilles quits the war; Thetis asks Zeus to avenge her son.
Zeus sends Agamemnon a false dream; Agamemnon tests the army and nearly loses it; the catalogue of the ships and their captains.
Paris and Menelaus fight a duel for Helen; Helen names the Greek chiefs from the wall; Aphrodite carries Paris off to safety.
The gods break the truce with an arrow from Pandarus; Agamemnon reviews his troops; the first day of battle begins.
The great day of Diomedes, who wounds two gods, Aphrodite and Ares, and drives them from the field.
Glaucus and Diomedes exchange armor instead of blows; Hector in Troy with his mother Hecuba, with Helen, and with his wife Andromache.
Hector and Ajax fight a duel to a draw; a truce to bury the dead; the Greeks build a wall around their ships.
Zeus forbids the gods to take part; the Trojans win the day and camp on the plain, their watchfires burning until dawn.
The embassy to Achilles: Agamemnon offers gifts and Briseis back; Odysseus, Phoenix, and Ajax plead with him, and he refuses.
A night raid: Odysseus and Diomedes catch the Trojan spy Dolon, kill King Rhesus in his sleep, and steal his horses.
Agamemnon's day of glory; Diomedes, Odysseus, and other Greek chiefs are wounded one by one; Nestor sends Patroclus to plead with Achilles.
The Trojans storm the Greek wall; Sarpedon tears down the rampart, and Hector smashes the gate with a boulder.
While Zeus looks away, Poseidon rallies the Greeks in disguise, and the battle for the ships hangs in the balance.
Hera seduces Zeus and lulls him to sleep; Poseidon turns the tide; Ajax fells Hector with a stone.
Zeus wakes and foretells the end of the war; Apollo levels the wall; Hector reaches the ships and calls for fire.
Patroclus fights in Achilles' armor, drives the Trojans from the ships, kills Sarpedon, and dies at Hector's hands.
The fight over the body of Patroclus; Hector puts on Achilles' armor; Achilles' immortal horses weep for the dead.
Achilles learns that Patroclus is dead and chooses vengeance over long life; Hephaestus forges him new armor and the great shield.
Achilles gives up his wrath against Agamemnon, who blames a goddess; Achilles arms for battle, and his horse foretells his death.
Zeus lets the gods into the fighting; Achilles returns to battle and meets Aeneas and Hector, whom the gods snatch to safety.
Achilles fills the river Scamander with the dead, and the river rises against him; the gods brawl; the Trojans flee inside the walls.
Hector waits alone outside the gates; Achilles chases him three times around the city and kills him; Priam, Hecuba, and Andromache mourn.
The ghost of Patroclus asks for burial; his funeral; the games held in his honor, from the chariot race to the spear-throw.
The gods order Hector's body returned; Priam crosses the plain at night to ransom his son from Achilles; the burial of Hector.
